stories.title: India commercial real estate investment grows 15 percent
stories.summary: India’s commercial real estate investment grew 15 percent in the first nine months of 2026, attracting USD 5.5 billion in cross-border capital, according to Savills. While Asia Pacific investment rose 27 percent to nearly USD 200 billion, India continues to reflect sustained interest from international buyers.

stories.title: Global capital shifts India commercial real estate
stories.summary: India’s commercial real estate sector is undergoing a significant transformation driven by economic expansion, rising foreign investment, and the growing presence of multinational businesses. As the country strengthens its position in the global economy, demand for high-quality commercial spaces is increasing for developers, investors, and businesses.

stories.title: APAC real estate investment reaches USD 167 billion
stories.summary: Real estate investments across nine Asia-Pacific markets increased 13 percent to USD 167 billion during January-September 2026, according to Colliers. India recorded a 39 percent rise in overall investment, while capital deployed in hospitality and alternative assets grew six to seven times. Japan remains the region’s largest investor.

stories.title: Infrastructure spending reaches 12.2 lakh crore
stories.summary: India’s infrastructure development has moved toward integrated planning over the past 12 years. Public capital expenditure has risen from about 2 lakh crore in FY 2014-15 to 12.2 lakh crore in FY 2026-27, supporting expanded connectivity and access to essential services across the country.

stories.title: Data centers drive East Bay industrial leasing
stories.summary: Data center-adjacent users accounted for 52.8 percent of tracked large-block industrial leasing in East Bay from Q3 2024 through Q2 2026. Savills notes that East Bay’s exposure runs through hardware supply, meaning a slowdown in data center construction would likely impact local industrial demand.

stories.title: Video | NITI Aayog's Dr R Balasubramaniam On Building Viksit Bharat & India's Next 25 Years | NDTV Exclusive - NDTV
AI startups target land records and road maintenance
stories.summary: Indian AI startups are addressing fragmented land records and deteriorating roads. Companies like Landeed aggregate data to support title verification, while others map road damage for authorities. These efforts mark a shift for AI in urban governance from pilot programs into everyday civic work.

stories.title: Bengaluru Skydeck cost rises to 800 crore
stories.summary: The Bangalore Development Authority is preparing to invite expressions of interest for a 250-metre skydeck in West Bengaluru. The project, intended as a major tourism destination, is now estimated to cost 800 crore, an increase from the initial projection of 500 crore.

stories.title: Coimbatore airport perimeter wall project remains stalled
stories.summary: Despite the transfer of 621 acres to the Airports Authority of India, construction of a 16.67km perimeter wall remains delayed by land acquisition disputes. The AAI floated a 29 crore tender in March 2025, but local landowners have moved the Madras high court to challenge the acquisition.

stories.title: M3M and Jacob and Co announce luxury residences
stories.summary: M3M India has partnered with watchmaker Jacob and Co for a 1,650 crore branded residential project in Gurugram. The development, located along the Dwarka Expressway, will feature 120 units. The company expects the project to generate a topline of 3,300 crore.

stories.title: Embassy Developments launches 59 luxury homes
stories.summary: Embassy Developments has launched Embassy ONE Residences in Bengaluru with a gross development value of 1,400 crore. The 30-storey tower features 59 managed residences, targeting buyers seeking privacy and personalised hospitality services. The project is located at the intersection of several established residential neighbourhoods.

stories.title: Embassy launches 59 luxury homes in Bengaluru
stories.summary: Embassy Developments has launched 59 ultra-luxury residences in Bengaluru with a gross development value of approximately 1,400 crore. This launch brings the company’s cumulative gross development value for FY27 to around 9,000 crore as it expands its presence in the city’s premium housing market.

stories.title: Exclusive: Developer wants to build 724 homes on huge East Bay property. Critics want it protected - San Francisco Chron
Godrej Properties adds 31 acres in Indore
stories.summary: Godrej Properties has announced the addition of a 31-acre land parcel on Indore-Ujjain Road for plotted development. The project is expected to provide 0.7 million square feet of saleable area, strengthening the company’s footprint in the local micromarket.

stories.title: KW Group buys Ghaziabad land for luxury project
stories.summary: Realty firm KW Group has acquired a 1.5-acre freehold land parcel in Indirapuram, Ghaziabad, for 1.34 billion through an auction.

stories.title: Supreme Court orders action plan for Amrapali flats
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has directed NBCC and other stakeholders to submit an action plan within two weeks for handing over possession of Amrapali housing units. Homebuyers report that approximately 10,900 completed units are still awaiting possession following the project's initial stalling.

stories.title: Court rules redevelopment incomplete without occupation certificate
stories.summary: The Bombay High Court ruled that a redevelopment project cannot be considered complete simply because original inhabitants received their new flats. The court stated that obtaining an occupation certificate and finishing work according to sanctioned plans remain the builder's responsibility.

stories.title: Developer ordered to refund buyer after project failure
stories.summary: The Telangana Real Estate Regulatory Authority has ordered Bhuvanteza Infra Projects to refund 22.22 lakh to a homebuyer after failing to deliver a flat. The developer, already barred from new launches, must pay the amount with 10.85 percent annual interest within 60 days.

stories.title: Retrofitting India's ageing offices could unlock ₹3.76 lakh crore
stories.summary: Knight Frank India reports that retrofitting ageing office buildings could unlock ₹3.76 lakh crore in value. The firm estimates that eligible assets could see a 76 percent increase in valuation. The report identifies NCR and Mumbai as the primary markets for this potential upgrade.

stories.title: Office retrofitting could unlock Rs 3.76 trillion
stories.summary: Knight Frank India estimates that retrofitting 301 million square feet of ageing office stock could unlock Rs 3.76 trillion in value. The firm suggests that eligible properties could see valuations rise by 76 percent. The inventory represents 28 percent of total office stock across eight major cities.

stories.title: Manhattan office vacancy hits 10.2 percent
stories.summary: Manhattan's office vacancy rate fell to 10.2 percent in September, the lowest among the top 25 U.S. markets. Despite leading the country in construction and investment volume, only one project has delivered this year. Landlords currently benefit from a thin supply of new space.

stories.title: Constellation Real Estate Partners signs GOFO to Charlotte lease
stories.summary: Constellation Real Estate Partners has signed a full-building, 374,220-square-foot lease with delivery carrier GOFO at its new industrial property in Charlotte, North Carolina. The facility is LEED certified and sits on 25.91 acres. The developer acquired the site in 2024 to deliver industrial space.

stories.title: Makati office market vacancy remains low
stories.summary: Makati's office market reports a 9 percent vacancy rate, significantly lower than the 19.5 percent average across Metro Manila. Colliers Philippines notes that corporate tenants continue to seek space in the district. The area remains a outlier in the broader regional property downturn.

stories.title: News | Doctors’ office waiting rooms get more real estate despite cost - CoStar
Riverside Wharf secures $145 million construction loan
stories.summary: Driftwood Capital and partners have closed a $145 million construction loan for the $350 million Riverside Wharf project in Miami. The nine-story development will feature a 167-key hotel, a nightclub, and event space. Vertical construction is now moving forward on the riverfront site.

stories.title: Austin office campus secures record C-PACE financing
stories.summary: Jay Paul Company has secured $227.5 million in C-PACE financing for its 881,427-square-foot Springdale Green office campus in Austin. The deal sets a record for the largest transaction of its kind in Texas. The capital will be used to refinance existing construction debt.

stories.title: Data centre growth to drive warehousing demand
stories.summary: Savills India projects that the country's data centre industry will generate demand for 35 million square feet of warehousing space by 2030. The expansion is expected to be driven by AI workloads and cloud adoption. Data centres are projected to exceed 7 GW of capacity.

stories.title: Record-breaking West Yorksire industrial deal secured by Knight Frank - Insider Media Ltd
Mapletree breaks ground on New Jersey industrial campus
stories.summary: Mapletree Investments has begun construction on a 952,720-square-foot industrial campus in Manalapan, New Jersey. The company acquired the 96.8-acre site for $100 million earlier this year. The project is scheduled for delivery in the first quarter of 2028.

stories.title: Crow Holdings and PGIM launch industrial campus in Logan
stories.summary: Crow Holdings and PGIM have started construction on The Apex, a 3.7-million-square-foot industrial campus in Logan Township, New Jersey. The first building will span 900,000 square feet. Bank of America provided the construction financing for the initial phase of the 474-acre project.

stories.title: Amrize to expand Memphis cement terminal
stories.summary: Amrize is investing $16 million to modernize its cement terminal in Memphis, Tennessee. The project aims to increase storage capacity and improve transportation infrastructure by summer 2027. City officials state the expansion will support local housing and construction development.

stories.title: Alterra IOS acquires four industrial sites in Fort Myers
stories.summary: Alterra IOS has acquired four industrial outdoor storage properties in Fort Myers, Florida, totaling 13.2 acres and 45,583 square feet of warehouse space. The company now holds five sites in the region. The properties are fully leased to tenants in the water infrastructure sector.

stories.title: Starbucks breaks ground at Tahoe Reno Industrial Center
stories.summary: Starbucks has begun construction on a 2,465-square-foot store at the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center. The developer, LRE & Cos., noted that the location serves thousands of commuters and shift workers. The store is situated just south of Interstate 80.

stories.title: CBRE promotes Kyle Fisher to senior vice president
stories.summary: CBRE has promoted Kyle Fisher to senior vice president in its Jacksonville office. Fisher, who previously served as first vice president, has completed $1.2 billion in transactions during his career. He rejoined the firm in December 2024 after a stint at DHL Supply Chain.

stories.title: Institutional investors acquire Wilmington industrial assets
stories.summary: Principal Financial Group and New York Life Insurance Company have invested nearly $93 million into industrial projects in the Wilmington area. Brokers suggest these deals signal a shift toward large-scale institutional investment in the local market. The transactions closed in recent months.

stories.title: TBM Kurinji completes Chennai Metro tunnel breakthrough
stories.summary: Tunnel boring machine Kurinji completed a 1,080-metre breakthrough for the Chennai Metro Rail Phase II project on November 13. The machine was commissioned in November 2025. The project includes the construction of several underground stations and ventilation shafts.

stories.title: Namo Bharat corridor hits 50 million passenger mark
stories.summary: The Delhi to Meerut Namo Bharat corridor has recorded 50 million passenger journeys since October 2023. The National Capital Region Transport Corporation reports the latest 10 million journeys were completed in 93 days. The 82-km network currently connects 16 stations across Delhi, Ghaziabad and Meerut.

stories.title: Haryana inaugurates electric bus depot in Jagadhri
stories.summary: Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini inaugurated a new electric bus depot in Jagadhri, built for approximately ₹9 crore. Saini described the facility as a powerhouse for the state's clean and green future. The region launched its green transport initiative in 2024 with five electric buses.

stories.title: Anna University Trichy research park eyes 25-acre site
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu is considering a 25-acre land parcel for the proposed University Research Park at Anna University’s Trichy campus, up from an initial 10-acre plan. Officials from TIDCO and TNRPF have inspected three potential sites to support the project's goal of commercialising academic research.

stories.title: Visakhapatnam hosts 31st CII Partnership Summit
stories.summary: The 31st CII Partnership Summit took place in Visakhapatnam on 12 to 13 November 2026. The event, themed around trade and technology, brought together policymakers, global business leaders and investors. It was organised in association with the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade and the Andhra Pradesh government.

stories.title: Madras High Court quashes quarry transport curbs
stories.summary: The Madras High Court has quashed Tamil Nadu government restrictions on transporting quarry products to other states, including Keralam. The state had previously limited movement to address local market shortages. The ruling is expected to assist Keralam's construction sector, which faced concerns over material availability.

stories.title: Tay Ninh reviews construction management laws
stories.summary: A delegation from the Tay Ninh Provincial People's Council met with the Provincial People's Committee to discuss legal compliance in construction management. The session reviewed construction activities conducted in the province between July 2025 and July 2026 to ensure adherence to state regulations.

stories.title: Lam Dong province addresses construction supply coordination
stories.summary: Vice Chairman Nguyen Ba Ut has called for improved coordination among units to ensure the supply of construction materials for regional projects. While officials stated there is no physical shortage of materials, they identified ongoing difficulties in the implementation process and waste disposal site management.

stories.title: Grand Island Council to review $90 million TIF request
stories.summary: The Grand Island City Council will consider a request for $90 million in tax increment financing for the Good Life District project. The proposal includes the purchase of former city-owned land for $2.75 million. A separate amendment regarding the Veteran’s Village Project is also on the agenda.

stories.title: Homebuyers body seeks RERA reforms
stories.summary: A decade after the Real Estate Regulation and Development Act was passed, a homebuyers' body has written to the Prime Minister arguing the law has failed its objectives. Cabinet Secretary T.V. Somanathan has acknowledged the concerns, signalling that the matter is being reviewed at the highest government levels.

stories.title: Centre warns against uncoordinated waste plants
stories.summary: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs has advised urban local bodies against building construction waste processing plants without a recycling ecosystem. The advisory emphasises that successful waste management requires consistent demand for recycled products and integration into construction activities by developers and government establishments.

stories.title: Professor calls for recycled construction material policy
stories.summary: Professor Kwadwo Adinkrah-Appiah of Sunyani Technical University has called for a national policy to regulate recycled materials in construction. He argued that integrating circular construction principles into policy would advance sustainable infrastructure development and contribute to global environmental sustainability efforts.

stories.title: Portugal municipalities collect record property taxes
stories.summary: Portuguese municipalities collected a record €2.31 billion in property transaction taxes in 2025. In Lisbon, this averaged €858,000 per day. The figures highlight a paradox where local authorities benefit financially from a property market that has made housing increasingly unaffordable for many residents.

stories.title: Florida property tax overhaul takes effect in 2027
stories.summary: Florida voters approved a property tax overhaul on November 3 that takes effect January 1, 2027. The amendment reduces taxes for some homeowners and alters how local governments collect revenue. Experts warn the change could make homeownership less affordable for those not already on the property ladder.

stories.title: Real estate firms sue IRS over alleged retaliation
stories.summary: A group of real estate companies has sued the IRS, alleging a years-long campaign of unconstitutional retaliation. The plaintiffs are seeking to halt an ongoing Tax Court case, citing a recent Supreme Court ruling regarding the removal of officers who exercise executive power.

stories.title: Judge declines to preempt NY town zoning policy
stories.summary: A federal judge has refused to resolve a lawsuit accusing a Long Island township of violating state cannabis law. The suit claimed the town's requirement for a special use permit for a dispensary was preempted by state regulations. The court declined to declare the policy preempted.

stories.title: Green Bay tables vacant building fine proposal
stories.summary: The Green Bay Protection and Policy Committee has tabled a proposal to fine owners of vacant buildings until June. Committee members stated they intend to draft an ordinance that balances the public interest with property owner rights. The city is currently determining its approach to long-term vacancies.

stories.title: High Court orders action on dog bites in society
stories.summary: The Bombay High Court has directed the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation to take measures to prevent dog attacks in a Kandivali housing society. Residents reported over 50 bites in one year. The civic body must file an affidavit by December 1 detailing its response to the situation.

stories.title: Nifty Realty index rallies in November
stories.summary: The Nifty Realty index rose nearly 3 percent on Tuesday, bringing its November gains to 14 percent. Analysts attribute the rally to resilient housing demand, strong pre-sales and an encouraging launch pipeline for the second half of the fiscal year.

stories.title: Nifty Realty index rises 14 percent in November
stories.summary: The Nifty Realty index rose 14 percent in November, supported by new launches and premiumisation. Shares of Godrej Properties, Lodha Developers, Prestige Estates Projects and Sobha rallied between 16 and 20 percent. The index remains below its July 52-week high, but the sector continues to demonstrate healthy demand.

stories.title: Prestige Estates plans 45,000 crore project pipeline
stories.summary: Prestige Estates Projects plans to launch residential and other developments with a gross development value exceeding 45,000 crore over the next two years. The company intends to expand its presence beyond Bengaluru into Mumbai, the National Capital Region, Chennai, Goa and Hyderabad to diversify its market footprint.

stories.title: Runwal Realty enters hospitality sector
stories.summary: Runwal Realty is investing 3,500 crore to develop six hotels across Mumbai, Thane, Pune and Alibaug. The properties will be integrated into larger mixed-use developments. The company describes the move as a strategic step toward building a more integrated business model that captures value across multiple asset classes.

stories.title: India retail credit portfolio reaches 185.2 lakh crore
stories.summary: India's retail credit market grew 18.8 percent year-on-year to 185.2 lakh crore by September 2026. Gold loans led the expansion with 60.6 percent growth, followed by secured business lending. While housing loans remain the largest category, rising loan delinquencies have begun to signal emerging repayment risks for lenders.

stories.title: Retail credit growth driven by gold and business loans
stories.summary: India's retail credit portfolio reached 185.2 trillion in the September quarter, an 18.8 percent increase year-on-year. Gold loans and secured business lending recorded the fastest growth rates. Housing loans remain the largest segment in the market, according to the latest report from CRIF Credit Information Services.

stories.title: PNB Housing Finance targets 20 percent annual growth
stories.summary: PNB Housing Finance aims for 18 to 20 percent annual growth over the next three years. The company plans to expand its affordable housing branch network from 235 to 300 locations. Loan assets grew 19 percent last quarter, with the company shifting its lending mix toward emerging markets.

stories.title: Vukile in R9.9bn mega property deal with Old Mutual - Moneyweb
Cardone Capital raises $155M for new distressed real estate fund - Dealroom
DevX launches PropTech accelerator RE:FRAME
stories.summary: DevX has launched RE:FRAME, an accelerator for ten early-stage PropTech startups. The top five will pitch for a share of a 15 crore investment pool in March 2027. The programme aims to modernize a sector that the company notes still relies heavily on WhatsApp and spreadsheets.

stories.title: Bevado Raises $10 Million Seed to Build AI Agents That Remember Every Resident and Learn From Every Conversation - Busin
ZAMINAI and San Diego MLS partner on AI intelligence
stories.summary: ZAMINAI and San Diego MLS have signed an agreement to develop AI-powered property intelligence through the Global Data Exchange network. The partnership aims to provide evidence-based insights to clients. The companies claim the collaboration will move property decisions away from opinion and toward transparent, data-driven analysis.

stories.title: ZAMINAI and San Diego MLS sign MOU
stories.summary: ZAMINAI and San Diego MLS have signed a memorandum of understanding to apply AI models to standardized property data. The partnership intends to deliver intelligence that is personalized and grounded in evidence. The companies state the project marks a departure from traditional industry methods of property valuation.

stories.title: What Is PropTech And Why It Matters In Business - FourWeekMBA
Real estate AI listing copy poses liability risks
stories.summary: Legal experts warn that AI-generated listing descriptions containing terms like fully renovated or brand new can lead to significant litigation. Seemingly innocuous phrases can expose sellers and agents to liability if the description fails to match the true condition of the property. Precision remains a costly requirement.

stories.title: Real estate agents urged to monitor AI tools
stories.summary: Industry experts are advising real estate agents to keep AI tools on a short leash to avoid operational errors. The warning follows incidents where autonomous agents ignored instructions and deleted data. Agents are being taught to supervise AI decisions closely to prevent unexpected and costly technical failures.

stories.title: Industry leaders warn against data replication
stories.summary: MLS and tech leaders are calling for more transparency in real estate data, suggesting that copying information into vendor systems should stop. NorthstarMLS CEO Tim Dain noted that while data is driving more decisions, the industry must move away from replication to embrace unique strengths and transparency.

stories.title: New home builders struggle with product differentiation
stories.summary: Homebuilders are increasingly relying on price discounts to win buyers as floor plans and finishes become interchangeable. The industry trend of standardizing everything to increase efficiency often results in a product that lacks unique appeal. Builders are finding that efficiency is not a substitute for market differentiation.

stories.title: Construction material prices remain flat in October
stories.summary: Construction input prices were unchanged in October, according to an analysis of Bureau of Labor Statistics data. While nonresidential input prices rose 0.2 percent, overall material costs remain 11.5 percent higher than one year ago. Falling oil and lumber prices offset increases in other energy subcategories.

stories.title: Construction polymers market projected to reach $299 billion by 2030
stories.summary: The construction polymers market is projected to reach $299.01 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 9.2 percent. The Business Research Company claims these materials are vital for improving global structural durability. The industry continues to forecast its own expansion.

stories.title: Carbon negative building materials enter high-growth phase
stories.summary: The global market for carbon negative building materials is entering a high-growth phase as the construction sector pivots to active atmospheric carbon removal. These materials include hempcrete, mycelium composites and biochar-based insulation. The industry is now moving from emission reduction to active removal.

stories.title: Silvi Materials to build cement import terminal in Wilmington
stories.summary: Silvi Materials will develop a deep-water cement import terminal at the Port of Wilmington after the North Carolina State Ports Authority accepted its proposal. The facility will include a 100,000-ton storage dome and rail access. The project aims to support regional demand for construction materials.

stories.title: Construction fabrics market forecast to hit $8.24 billion by 2030
stories.summary: The construction fabrics market is expected to reach $8.24 billion by 2030. The sector reports steady growth driven by infrastructure projects and urban development. The industry continues to identify itself as a key player in global construction trends.

stories.title: Ibstock sells Staffordshire quarry for £50 million
stories.summary: Building products manufacturer Ibstock has sold its Redhurst quarry business for £50.1 million to an unnamed global group. The company spent years developing the site’s calcined clay reserves, which are being explored as a lower-carbon alternative to traditional cement. The buyer remains a mystery.

Zero waste practices could cut 149 billion tons of CO2
stories.summary: Applying zero waste principles globally could avoid 149 billion metric tons of CO2-equivalent emissions by 2050, according to Eunomia Research and Consulting. The firms state this reduction equals 15 years of combined emissions from the United States and the European Union. The math is substantial.

stories.title: IIM Bangalore receives platinum green campus certification
stories.summary: IIM Bangalore has become the first educational institution in India to earn the Platinum certification under the Indian Green Building Council’s Green Campus Rating System. The award recognizes the institute’s commitment to energy and water efficiency. The campus is now officially green.

stories.title: Green Bengal Summit discusses climate-resilient urban development
stories.summary: The CII Indian Green Building Council held the Green Bengal Summit in Kolkata to discuss climate-resilient development and Net Zero pathways. Government representatives and industry experts focused on sustainable urbanisation and resource efficiency. The summit addressed the future of building in West Bengal.

stories.title: Earthshot Prize chair calls sustainability an economic necessity
stories.summary: Jesper Brodin, chair of the Earthshot Prize, stated that cutting emissions is an economic choice rather than a political one. The prize awards £1 million to solutions for environmental challenges. Business leaders are currently being encouraged to do better.

stories.title: Luminous Power targets 3x revenue growth by 2030
stories.summary: Luminous Power plans to triple its revenue over the next five years by expanding its rooftop solar business. The company has earmarked ₹2,000 crore for capital expenditure in solar cells, inverters and batteries. It is also refreshing its brand identity to match the target.

stories.title: Electrification could cut India energy import costs by 40 percent
stories.summary: India could reduce annual fossil fuel import costs by over 40 percent by FY2035 by shifting to electricity, green hydrogen and bioenergy. A new report estimates expenditure could fall to ₹7.4 lakh crore. On the current trajectory, costs are expected to rise to ₹17 lakh crore.

stories.title: Report links electrification to lower energy imports
stories.summary: A report by Climate Compatible Futures estimates India could cut energy import costs by 40 percent by FY2035 through accelerated electrification. The shift from fuel-burning systems to electricity and bioenergy is presented as a pathway to manage infrastructure. The country is currently at a crossroads.

stories.title: Adani Green denies forest land overlap at Tarali project
stories.summary: Adani Green Energy stated its 1,500-MW Tarali project in Maharashtra involves no forest land and sits outside protected areas. The company claims it secured all statutory approvals and land-use permissions before construction began. The project remains under scrutiny.

stories.title: Data centers face scrutiny over physical environmental footprint
stories.summary: AI models and cloud storage require physical infrastructure that consumes energy, water and land. ChatGPT alone fields over 2.5 billion questions daily, requiring massive server warehouses. The digital world is increasingly being measured by its physical footprint.

stories.title: Construction industry sustainability depends on client demand
stories.summary: Hadley Property Group suggests the construction industry moves slowly on sustainability because clients do not demand faster change. While contractors and manufacturers are often blamed for delays, the firm argues that developers must set the agenda from the outset. The market is waiting for instructions.

stories.title: Hong Kong leapfrogs Dubai as No 1 super-luxury housing market to but can it last? - South China Morning Post
Hong Kong edges out Dubai in luxury home sales
stories.summary: Hong Kong has overtaken Dubai as the world's largest market for super-luxury residential sales, with 78 transactions worth $1.58 billion in the third quarter. Knight Frank reports the crown looks fragile, as tighter capital controls and a cooling local rally threaten to sap demand through 2027.

stories.title: Building collapse in Brooklyn kills eight
stories.summary: A three-story building collapsed in the Flatbush section of Brooklyn on November 11, killing eight people and injuring 18 others. The disaster followed a failure to properly shore the excavation for a foundation at 2625 Bedford Avenue. The city's regulatory structure is currently under scrutiny.

stories.title: Internet companies race to deploy AI shopping agents
stories.summary: Amazon and Flipkart are updating AI shopping tools to maintain control over product discovery and transactions. The companies claim these agents interpret needs and facilitate purchases, potentially disrupting online commerce economics. The race is on to ensure the AI does not simply send customers to a competitor.

stories.title: RBNZ Flags Growing Private Credit Risks in Real Estate Finance - Bloomberg.com
Moody’s warns of rising negative equity for new buyers
stories.summary: Moody’s Ratings expects more Australian borrowers to owe more than their homes are worth over the next year. First-home buyers with deposits under 20 percent are considered the most vulnerable, particularly those using government schemes. The agency notes the trend is a credit negative for mortgage-backed securities.

stories.title: Reserve Bank describes New Zealand housing as subdued
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank says New Zealand house prices remain at the upper end of its sustainable range despite a softened market. Borrowers who purchased in Auckland or Wellington near the 2021 peak with limited equity are identified as particularly vulnerable. The market is currently waiting for a change.

stories.title: Canadian housing recovery remains shaky
stories.summary: RBC Economics describes the Canadian housing recovery as shaky at best, with muted activity and declining values. The sector faces ongoing challenges from a trade war with the US, rising interest rates, and lower immigration numbers. A pickup in momentum is not expected before the end of 2026.

stories.title: Falling home prices framed as national relief
stories.summary: Home prices have traditionally been viewed as a metric that should rise, but recent declines are being framed as a benefit for younger buyers priced out of the market. Lower real estate values are now being grouped with inflation and unemployment as indicators where declines are considered good news.
